Source: none. This notebook audits the sample-definition stage: the drop of
Mojuí dos Campos, the 2000-2003 baseline summaries, the forest-availability
floor and the two at-risk gates, the window-consistent PPCDAm treatment
flags and the cross-sectional pressure scores, with the positivity and
balance diagnostics that the legacy script printed to the console.
Pipeline script: `_scripts/05-sample-definition.R`.
Interim outputs: `_data/interim/panel_amz_2000_2020_sample.rds` and
`_data/interim/panel_amz_baseline.rds`.
Equivalence with the recovered panel is not checked here (the notebook never
reads `_data/reference/`); the `compare_outputs` report lives in the phase 1
script 05 commit message and in the decision entries it cites.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
})
options(width = 110)
```

```{r read}
panel_in <- read_rds("_data/interim/panel_amz_2000_2020.rds")
panel <- read_rds("_data/interim/panel_amz_2000_2020_sample.rds")
muni <- read_rds("_data/interim/panel_amz_baseline.rds")
BASE_YEARS <- 2000:2003
WINDOWS <- tibble(window = c("main", "robust"), treat = c("ppcdam_main",
                  "ppcdam_robust"), start = 2004L, end = c(2010L, 2012L))
```

## Q1. What does the drop of Mojuí dos Campos remove, and is every remaining municipality observed over the baseline window?

What is checked: the rows the drop removes, Mojuí's non-missing
baseline-window cells in the columns the sample rule reads, and the count of
baseline years per remaining municipality for the deforestation area.

```{r q1-mojui}
panel_in %>%
  filter(geocode == "1504752", year %in% BASE_YEARS) %>%
  summarise(rows = n(),
            across(c(deforestation_area_km2, forest_area_km2, munic_area_km2,
                     cattle_per_km2, crop_soy_munic_area_share, ppcdam_list),
                   ~ sum(!is.na(.x))))
```

```{r q1-baseline-years}
panel %>%
  filter(year %in% BASE_YEARS) %>%
  group_by(geocode) %>%
  summarise(years = sum(!is.na(deforestation_area_km2)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  count(years)
```

**Finding.** The drop removes Mojuí's 21 rows (503 to 502 municipalities).
Over 2000-2003 the municipality carries deforestation, forest, area and the
PPCDAm indicator (never listed) but no cattle or crop values, so its
baseline clearing would exist while its agricultural pressure would not;
the substantive reason for the drop is the absence of every social and
economic series before 2013 (`_audit/panel.qmd` Q7). Every remaining
municipality has four baseline years of deforestation area.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-l (provisional; issue #8).
**Assertion.** `05-sample-definition.R`, raw-state block (Mojuí present
in the input, no NA in the deforestation, forest and area columns) and
output block (502 municipalities, Mojuí absent).

## Q2. Which municipalities lack a baseline covariate, and how are the baselines distributed?

What is checked: NA counts in the municipality file; the municipalities with
a missing baseline; quantiles of the five baseline measures.

```{r q2-na}
muni %>%
  summarise(across(c(defor_area_b, defor_rate_b, cattle_dens_b, crop_share_b,
                     forest_share_2000, pressure_defor, pressure_agri,
                     pressure_score, avail_ok, at_risk_broad, at_risk_narrow),
                   ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "na_munic") %>%
  filter(na_munic > 0)
```

```{r q2-which}
muni %>%
  filter(is.na(cattle_dens_b) | is.na(crop_share_b)) %>%
  select(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation, defor_area_b,
         cattle_dens_b, crop_share_b, forest_share_2000, avail_ok,
         at_risk_narrow, ppcdam_robust)
```

```{r q2-quantiles}
muni %>%
  select(defor_area_b, defor_rate_b, cattle_dens_b, crop_share_b,
         forest_share_2000) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "baseline") %>%
  group_by(baseline) %>%
  summarise(min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            p10 = quantile(value, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            p90 = quantile(value, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(-baseline, ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

**Finding.** Three municipalities have no agricultural baseline: Ipiranga
do Norte and Itanhangá (MT) have no PAM or PPM rows before their first
survey year (D-2026-10-10-g), and Santa Cruz do Arari (PA) has no crop
series at all (D-2026-10-10-i). Their `pressure_agri` and
`pressure_score` are NA; their flags are defined because the flags read
only clearing and forest share. The baselines are right-skewed, which is
why the pressure scores log them first. The 2000 forest share exceeds 1
for one municipality, Nova Ubiratã (1.18), the mesh-vintage mismatch of
`_audit/panel.qmd` Q3 (task 1.8); it passes the floor either way.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-12-a (NA, never NaN, where a source has no baseline
value).
**Assertion.** `05-sample-definition.R`, output block
(`N_AGRI_NA_EXPECTED` = 3, no NA in clearing and forest share, flags never
NA).

## Q3. Which municipalities count as treated under each analysis window?

What is checked: listed municipalities by year, first-listing cohorts, exits
within the robust window, and the treated counts under the main (2004-2010),
robust (2004-2012) and full-panel definitions.

```{r q3-cohorts}
panel %>%
  filter(ppcdam_list == 1L) %>%
  group_by(geocode) %>%
  summarise(first = min(year), last = max(year), .groups = "drop") %>%
  count(first, name = "cohort_size")
```

```{r q3-exits}
panel %>%
  filter(year >= 2004, year <= 2012) %>%
  group_by(geocode) %>%
  summarise(listed_years = sum(ppcdam_list),
            exited = any(ppcdam_list == 1L) &&
              ppcdam_list[year == 2012] == 0L, .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(exited) %>%
  left_join(select(muni, geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation),
            by = "geocode")
```

```{r q3-counts}
muni %>%
  summarise(main = sum(ppcdam_main), robust = sum(ppcdam_robust),
            ever_full = sum(ppcdam_ever_full))
```

**Finding.** Listing starts in 2008 (36 municipalities) with a second
cohort in 2009 (7), so the main window holds 43 treated municipalities and
no exit; 2011 and 2012 add 8, so the robust window holds 51, and six of
its treated municipalities (four in Pará, two in Mato Grosso) have left
the list by 2012. Later cohorts (2017, 2018) bring the full-panel count to
61. A municipality first listed after a window's end is a control in that
design.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-12-b.
**Assertion.** `05-sample-definition.R`, output block (43, 51, 61; main
within robust within ever).

## Q4. Does the at-risk restriction remove treated municipalities?

What is checked: for each window, the number of municipalities, treated and
control, in the full sample and under the broad and narrow gates.

```{r q4-retention}
retention <- function(d, treat) {
  tibble(
    sample  = c("full", "avail", "broad", "narrow"),
    n       = c(nrow(d), sum(d$avail_ok), sum(d$at_risk_broad),
                sum(d$at_risk_narrow)),
    treated = c(sum(d[[treat]]), sum(d[[treat]] & d$avail_ok),
                sum(d[[treat]] & d$at_risk_broad),
                sum(d[[treat]] & d$at_risk_narrow))
  ) %>%
    mutate(control = n - treated)
}
map_dfr(set_names(WINDOWS$treat, WINDOWS$window), ~ retention(muni, .x),
        .id = "window")
```

**Finding.** Under both windows every treated municipality survives the
floor and both gates; the restriction removes controls only, from 459 to
425 (broad) and 365 (narrow) in the main window and from 451 to 417 and
357 in the robust window. The floor alone removes two never-listed
Tocantins municipalities (Arapoema and Bernardo Sayão, forest share
below 0.09).
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-h (gates as inherited).
**Assertion.** `05-sample-definition.R`, output block (500, 468, 408;
every robust-window treated municipality in the narrow sample).

## Q5. Which baseline covariates differ between treated and control municipalities?

What is checked: treated and control means and the standardized mean
difference (difference over the pooled within-group standard deviation) for
five baseline covariates, by window and sample. The restriction is not
expected to balance covariates; the table names what matching or weighting
inside the at-risk sample must condition on (absolute values above about
0.1).

```{r q5-smd}
bal_covs <- c("forest_share_2000", "defor_area_b", "defor_rate_b",
              "cattle_dens_b", "crop_share_b")
smd_tab <- function(d, treat, label) {
  t <- d[d[[treat]] == 1L, ]
  c <- d[d[[treat]] == 0L, ]
  tibble(
    sample = label, covariate = bal_covs,
    mean_treated = map_dbl(bal_covs, ~ mean(t[[.x]], na.rm = TRUE)),
    mean_control = map_dbl(bal_covs, ~ mean(c[[.x]], na.rm = TRUE)),
    smd = map_dbl(bal_covs, function(v) {
      s <- sqrt((var(t[[v]], na.rm = TRUE) + var(c[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)) / 2)
      (mean(t[[v]], na.rm = TRUE) - mean(c[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)) / s
    })
  )
}
smd_by_window <- function(treat) {
  bind_rows(smd_tab(muni, treat, "full"),
            smd_tab(filter(muni, at_risk_broad), treat, "broad"),
            smd_tab(filter(muni, at_risk_narrow), treat, "narrow")) %>%
    mutate(across(c(mean_treated, mean_control, smd), ~ round(.x, 3)))
}
smd_by_window("ppcdam_main") %>% print(n = 15)
smd_by_window("ppcdam_robust") %>% print(n = 15)
```

**Finding.** Listed municipalities have far higher baseline clearing area
(smd about 1.5 in the main window, 1.4 in the robust one), are more
forested (0.7 to 0.9) and have lower clearing rate and cattle density
(about -0.4 to -0.6); the imbalance does not shrink as the sample narrows.
Crop share is balanced in the main window and tilts towards the treated
group (0.14 to 0.19) in the robust window, whose 2011-2012 cohorts are more
crop-oriented. These are the covariates the estimator conditions on.
**Decision.** none required; evidence for the chapter's methods section.
**Assertion.** none.

## Q6. Do treated and control municipalities share a region of common support?

What is checked: a logistic model of listing on the 2000 forest share and
the logged baseline clearing, cattle density and crop share; the overlap of
the two groups' propensity ranges; the units outside it, by window and
sample. Municipalities with a missing covariate are dropped from the model.

```{r q6-overlap}
ps_covs <- c("forest_share_2000", "log_defor_area_b", "log_cattle_dens_b",
             "log_crop_share_b")
ps_overlap <- function(d, treat, label) {
  cc <- d[complete.cases(d[ps_covs]), ]
  m <- glm(reformulate(ps_covs, response = treat), data = cc,
           family = binomial)
  cc$ps <- predict(m, type = "response")
  tr <- cc$ps[cc[[treat]] == 1L]
  co <- cc$ps[cc[[treat]] == 0L]
  lo <- max(min(tr), min(co))
  hi <- min(max(tr), max(co))
  tibble(sample = label, n = nrow(cc), treated = length(tr),
         support_lo = round(lo, 3), support_hi = round(hi, 3),
         off_support_treated = sum(tr < lo | tr > hi),
         off_support_control = sum(co < lo | co > hi),
         treated_median_ps = round(median(tr), 3),
         control_median_ps = round(median(co), 3))
}
overlap_by_window <- function(treat) {
  bind_rows(ps_overlap(muni, treat, "full"),
            ps_overlap(filter(muni, at_risk_broad), treat, "broad"),
            ps_overlap(filter(muni, at_risk_narrow), treat, "narrow"))
}
overlap_by_window("ppcdam_main")
overlap_by_window("ppcdam_robust")
```

**Finding.** The groups separate sharply: the median listed municipality
has a propensity near 0.7 against near zero for controls. Most controls in
the full sample lie below the treated range; the gates cut that off-support
mass (main window: 410 to 377 to 317; robust: 357 to 324 to 264) while
keeping every treated municipality. A residual block of listed
municipalities (14 main, 12 robust) sits above the control range: extreme
frontier units with no close control, to be reported with that caveat.
Three municipalities leave the model for missing covariates (Q2).
**Decision.** none required; evidence for the chapter's methods section.
**Assertion.** none.

## Q7. Are the pressure scores standardized, and how much do they depend on the sample?

What is checked: the moments of the three scores over the 502
municipalities, and the scores recomputed with the standardization run on
the broad at-risk sample only, as the governing rule for derived variables
would require if the scores were built in an analysis script.

```{r q7-moments}
muni %>%
  summarise(across(c(pressure_defor, pressure_agri, pressure_score),
                   list(mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        sd = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("score", "stat"),
               names_pattern = "(.*)_(mean|sd)$") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(across(c(mean, sd), ~ round(.x, 4)))
```

```{r q7-sample-dependence}
z <- function(x) (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
muni %>%
  filter(at_risk_broad) %>%
  mutate(defor_broad = z(log_defor_area_b),
         agri_broad = 0.5 * z(log_cattle_dens_b) +
           0.5 * z(log_crop_share_b),
         score_broad = z(defor_broad + agri_broad)) %>%
  summarise(max_shift_defor = max(abs(defor_broad - pressure_defor)),
            max_shift_agri = max(abs(agri_broad - pressure_agri),
                                 na.rm = TRUE),
            max_shift_score = max(abs(score_broad - pressure_score),
                                  na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

**Finding.** `pressure_defor` and `pressure_score` have mean 0 and sd 1
over the 502 municipalities; `pressure_agri` is a half-half mix of two
z-scores and has sd below 1 by construction. Restandardizing on the broad
at-risk sample moves the scores by up to 0.4 standard deviations, which
is the sample dependence the governing rule for derived variables
excludes from the panel.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-12-c (reproduced as inherited; flagged for the
storage audit, task 2.2).
**Assertion.** `05-sample-definition.R`, output block (moments of
`pressure_defor` and `pressure_score` within `Z_TOL`).

## Q8. Why does Santa Cruz do Arari's availability flag differ from the recovered panel?

What is checked: the municipality's baseline row. The recovered panel
carries no municipal area for it (D-2026-10-10-i), so its forest share
could not be computed there, and its availability flag reads FALSE; the
rebuilt panel has the area restored.

```{r q8-santa-cruz}
muni %>%
  filter(geocode == "1506401") %>%
  select(municipality, defor_area_b, cattle_dens_b, crop_share_b,
         forest_km2_2000, forest_share_2000, avail_ok, at_risk_broad,
         at_risk_narrow, pressure_defor, pressure_agri)
```

**Finding.** With the restored area the municipality's 2000 forest share
is 0.94 and it passes the floor; with zero baseline clearing it stays
outside both gates, as in the recovered panel, so the change touches
`avail_ok` only (21 cells). The recovered FALSE has no derivation from a
missing share (`NA >= 0.10` is NA, not FALSE), so the reference value is
treated as a legacy artefact and the rebuilt value accepted.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-12-d.
**Assertion.** `05-sample-definition.R`, output block
(`N_AVAIL_EXPECTED` = 500).
